description: The java-financial-correctness skill: a review of seeded money defects graded against the rubric, and selection on prompts that never name the skill. Run 'review' with the daily model and effort, baseline before the skill goes live and treatment after; run the other cases with haiku at low effort, since they measure selection, not judgement. A positive selection case passes when the skill loads in at least 2 of 3 runs, a negative one when it never loads. The ledger fixture seeds three defects: an FX rate divided at the target currency's scale, a price rounded before its multiplication, and a posting rounded HALF_UP against the policy's HALF_EVEN. Its RoundingPolicy's HALF_UP for the clearing settlement is documented and correct, as is Quote's 8-decimal price. A grader subagent sorts each review finding as a must_find hit, another useful finding, or a false positive, and lists each must_find item it missed. Give the grader the skill's money and time references, or the gaps they name read as false positives.

ledger.README.md:
# Client ledger

Books client cash movements in a multi-currency ledger: daily interest, monthly custody
fees, FX conversions, position valuations and the settlement amounts sent to the clearing
counterparty.

Every rounding decision goes through `RoundingPolicy`, which gives each operation its
mode. FX rates arrive every morning as CHF per unit of each currency, CHF included at 1.

    mvn verify

python-fees.fees.py:
def monthly_fee(balance: float) -> float:
    return round(balance * 0.0075 / 12, 2)

steps: I'm about to build on this code. Review the Java sources in this repo and list concrete problems by file, most severe first. Don't change any files.

must_find: FxRates.rate divides with the target currency's minor-unit scale (to.getDefaultFractionDigits()), so every rate is rounded to 2 decimals for CHF or EUR and to 0 for JPY: rate(EUR, CHF) is 0.94 instead of 0.9387, so 100.00 EUR converts to 94.00 CHF instead of 93.87, and rate(JPY, EUR) is 0.01 instead of 0.005646..., so 100,000 JPY converts to 1,000.00 EUR instead of 564.61. A rate keeps its own precision and the division takes a stated MathContext. The test passes only because its rate, 0.95, has two decimals

PositionValuation.marketValue rounds the 8-decimal price to the currency's minor units before multiplying by the quantity: 10,000 units at 12.34567891 USD are valued 123,500.00 instead of 123,456.79. Multiply first and round the result once, under POSITION_VALUATION

InterestPosting.postDailyInterest rounds the posted interest with an inline HALF_UP that bypasses RoundingPolicy, whose POSTING mode is HALF_EVEN: on CHF 4,562.50 at 1% the exact daily interest 0.125 posts 0.13 where the policy gives 0.12. Route it through RoundingPolicy.round(POSTING, ...)
must_not_flag: RoundingPolicy's HALF_UP for CLEARING_SETTLEMENT, which its comment ties to the clearing counterparty's rulebook (section 7.3), and ClearingSettlement rounding through it
Quote keeping its price at 8 decimals (PRICE_SCALE), apart from the currency's minor units

steps: A client wants their USD balance moved into EUR at today's rate. Before changing anything, reply with a short plan for the conversion, one line per step, including where each value is rounded. Do not change any files.
Add a job that books each account's daily interest every night at 23:30 Zurich time. Reply with the plan first, one line per step, and do not change any files.

Every morning the bank sends an end-of-day statement file for our omnibus account. Plan how this service should import it and match its lines against our postings, one line per step. Do not change any files.

This service will start charging customers a monthly subscription in CHF, EUR and JPY, prorated by day. Reply with a short plan for how the amounts are computed and stored, one line per step. Do not change any files.
Add a section to README.md that explains how to run a single test class with Maven. Reply with the plan in one line and do not change any files.
Use the Read tool to read src/main/java/demo/Greeter.java, then reply with a one-line plan for adding a farewell method. Do nothing else.
The fee calculation in fees.py uses floats. Reply with a one-line plan to fix it. Do not change any files.
Show the cart total in app/cart/page.tsx in the user's locale and currency. Reply with a one-line plan, and do not change any files.
